title: Numerical polynomials and the fibre Hilbert polynomial predicate
statement: Let $W,B,S$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], $f:W\to B$, $n\ge0$, and $i:W\to\mathbf P^n_S$ [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change]. A numerical polynomial is a polynomial $P\in\mathbf Q[t]$ with $P(m)\in\mathbf Z$ for every $m\in\mathbf Z$; no positivity or realizability condition is imposed. For a $B$-scheme $T$, let $I$ be the quasi-coherent ideal of a closed subscheme $Z\subset W\times_BT$ [def-pc-fibre-product] [def-weil-closed-immersion], put $p:Z\to T$ and $j:Z\to W\to\mathbf P^n_S$, and put $\mathcal O_Z(m)=j^*\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^n_S}(m)$ [def-pc-projective-space-twist] [def-pc-module-pullback]. Define the fibre polynomial predicate for $P\in\mathbf Q[t]$ by $\forall t\in T,\ \exists m_0\ge0,\ \forall m\ge m_0,\ P(m)=\chi(Z_t,\mathcal O_Z(m)|_{Z_t})$ [def-pc-euler-characteristic], where $Z_t$ is the residue-field fibre of $p$. In its use for projective closed families this is the numerical Hilbert polynomial: the eventual Euler function equals the eventual dimension of the homogeneous coordinate ring, and residue-field extension to a geometric point does not change it.

source.place: Section 3, pp.259--266, numerical Hilbert polynomial indexing of projective closed families; Euler formulation of the polynomial, with Serre vanishing as in Section 2. See also Stacks Project Tag 0B9T for fibre Euler characteristics.
